script: My sister's boyfriend is a man‑baby—so I used her towel to wipe the sink.. It started on a Monday, the same day I had just finished the laundry cycle and the dishes were still hanging in the sink. I am 24, my sister is 28 and doing a medical specialization, so she's basically a ghost in the house. I am the only one doing all the chores, so I expect a bit of respect for the space. Her boyfriend, a 27‑year‑old woman who's a complete manbaby, rolls into the apartment three times a week. Every single time she uses the sink, the entire countertop gets drenched. Like, literally water everywhere. The floor sometimes gets wet too. I stare at the wet mess, my patience slipping. I tried talking to my sister, asking her to tell him to dry the counter after he uses it. She said he'd just forget because he has ADHD. Classic excuse. So every time I see that soggy countertop, I grab her towel—because it's already there—and wipe the sink and floor dry. I don't bother with a cleaning rag; that's too much work. She doesn't know I am doing it and probably would flip out if I mentioned it, but honestly, I am not even mad. I do all the chores because she's out at the hospital, and I'd just like a little courtesy. And that's the tea: a manbaby boyfriend, a wet sink, and me drying it with my sister's towel, all while I am the one keeping the apartment clean. The audacity, right?
